definition: Contusion means a bruise caused by a blow.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word contusion. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know contusion should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: A contusion the size of a plum bloomed where the cabinet door had caught her forearm.
A scrape is far milder than a contusion — it takes the skin's top layer and is forgotten inside a week, while a contusion bleeds quietly under skin that held.
A break goes further than a contusion — a contusion bleeds quietly under skin that held; a break reaches the bone beneath it.

Bruise is the everyday, kitchen-table word for the mark a blow leaves — blood let loose under skin that held. A contusion is the same injury in chart language: the clinical term the report uses when precision matters. You show a friend the bruise; the radiologist writes contusion.

A shiner is slang for one particular bruise — the black eye, and only the black eye. A contusion can bloom anywhere a blow lands: forearm, hip, shin. Around the eye, described over the kitchen table, a contusion turns into a shiner; everywhere else it keeps the clinical name.
the mark's slow undoing
tissue whole and unmarked

Latin tundere, 'to pound,' left almost nothing else behind in English. Its one common survivor is obtuse — an angle or a mind pounded blunt — which this course teaches on its own card, so contusion has no new relative to hand you here. Remember the pounding instead: a contusion is the mark it leaves.

When a corner kick ricocheted off Lena's thigh in the final minute, the mark it left was deep purple and tender to the touch by bedtime.
At the clinic the next morning, the doctor pressed gently around its edges, asked her to bend her knee, and typed one line into the chart: contusion of the right thigh, skin intact.
Lena read the word over his shoulder and asked whether it meant something worse than she thought.
The doctor smiled and said the chart was describing what she already knew: a blow had broken tiny vessels beneath the surface, blood had pooled there, and the skin itself had stayed whole.
Nothing was torn and nothing was broken; the record simply wanted the precise term.
She left with an ice pack, orders to rest, and a small pride that her ordinary mark had earned such an official name.
